reason: Both correctly identified overheat protection and linked it to the new drawer, but Conversation 2 gathered more of the key unknowns (error code, pan type, recovery after cooling) and, when the homeowner refused to check underneath, gave an escalation route to an engineer, matching the expected path. Conversation 1 ended in a dead end: after the refusal it simply said 'we have to assume' the drawer is the cause and to stop using high, with no installer/engineer referral or next step, and it never asked about the flashing code. Conversation 2 has real flaws - a redundant repeat test, an unsupported 'pan misuse' heading, an irrelevant replacement-part panel, and framing the engineer visit around a 'failed fan' - which keep the margin slight.
